rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap LXXXVI His Majestie Forces out of Ireland
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly asks whether the King will procure troops from Ireland to harm Parliament.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A named wartime source question, not an independently verified forecast.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If Queen then North advance Army
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A second question asks whether the Queen, then in the north, will march with her army.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate from the Irish troops question.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A third question concerns whether the Queen's advance will succeed.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Advancing does not imply winning.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A fourth question asks when the Queen and King will meet.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Timing target distinct from whether she advances.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: square figure no explicit clock date
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A square horoscope accompanies the chapter without a clearly printed calendar date or clock time in its center.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Do not borrow the dated November 1642 figure from preceding Rupert chapter.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly assigns the King to Moon in Cancer in the tenth house.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source asserts a political-horary signifier rather than King's natal Moon.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes the Moon as increasing in light.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate from positional dignity.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Moon is elevated in tenth and in its own sign.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Accidental and essential dignities combined.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: void of all infelicity except slow motion
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He considers the Moon free of misfortune apart from slow motion.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Explicit source exception should not be dropped.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He interprets the chart as showing the King presently in a capable position.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Author reports this also reflected reality, without separate contemporaneous evidence.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Sun as eleventh lord signifies military assistance, commanders and men.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Technical assignment dependent on the figure.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Sun is placed in the seventh house in exaltation.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical planetary dignities; no separate ephemeris reconstruction.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun applies to a trine to the cusp of the eleventh.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Cusp aspect, not simply Moon-to-Sun trine.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The trine is approximately six degrees short of partile.
rules.original_source_qualifications: This is a stated degree separation, not six months/days.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in own house well fortified
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon's strength is invoked as further support for the King's forces.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Repeated testimony is not another independent observation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly judges that the King will obtain assistance from commanders and soldiers from Ireland.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Arrival is a different endpoint from winning or effectively using the aid.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Sun and Moon are considered favorable toward the King's significator.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Broad horary relationship.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun in seventh direct opposition ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Sun as auxiliary military force occupies the seventh, directly opposing the ascendant.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The ascendant represents the parliamentary side.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts Irish troops would harm Parliament.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No objective extent or time threshold stated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says the Sun is near the descending lunar node.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Unverified celestial proximity and historical malefic convention.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He invokes the Sun's sinister square toward the tenth-house cusp.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate from its favorable eleventh trine.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly fears the Irish help will create scandal for the King and his party.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Reputational harm distinct from battlefield losses.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He anticipates negative reports resulting from the reinforcements.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A broad, unmeasured public-information endpoint.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: improve Forces augment for certain time
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects the Irish aid to increase the King's military forces temporarily.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Temporary enhancement not equivalent to lasting tactical success.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts the reinforcements will not maintain their effectiveness for long.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No exact duration provided.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He explains nonpersistence by saying neither light is in a fixed sign.
rules.original_source_qualifications: An additional purported rule for duration.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says troops arrived from Ireland.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Reported after the question, not an independently authenticated military roll here.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims their arrival increased English hostility to the King.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historically partisan interpretation, not an independently measured opinion shift.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says their effectiveness was ended.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No independent chronicle provided in this source batch.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes their defeat or dispersal to Fairfax's forces at Nantwich.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Specific named retrospective military episode, not a second prospective forecast.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Queen is represented by Saturn.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A different significator than the King's Moon.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is said to rule the fourth house, the seventh from the King's tenth house.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Derived house is a stated source method.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is approaching movement from one zodiac sign to another.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source employs sign change as motion signal.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author stresses Saturn is a slow or weighty planet.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Used interpretively with ingress, not literal marching speed.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts the Queen will advance with her forces.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from advancing successfully.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He anticipates the Queen's intention to meet the King.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Intention cannot be independently confirmed from horoscope alone.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon wants three four degrees trine Saturn
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is said to be three or four degrees from applying trine to Saturn.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The numerical-degree condition controls timing.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: three or four months from Figure
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly predicts the Queen would approach the King about three or four months after the figure.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The chapter's figure does not clearly print a date; cannot independently convert to a calendar deadline.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: King great desire to see her
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author reads Moon applying to the Queen's Saturn as royal longing for reunion.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Unverified psychological interpretation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He states they met around 14 July 1643.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Explicit historical date in retrospective narrative, not validated against another witness.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He places the meeting in Warwickshire.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate geographic claim without external authentication.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: cannot compare months without question date
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source supplies a relative forecast window and later claimed meeting date but not a clearly dated question figure.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Do not use a previous chapter's November 1642 date to manufacture a miss or hit.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: she should not prosper but decline
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly judges that the Queen would not prosper despite advancing.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A negative endpoint distinct from marching and reunion.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He bases this on Saturn entering Aries, which he treats as its fall.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Prospective change of dignity is a condition.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter, a benefic, is described as separated from Saturn.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separation rather than future help.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He interprets the separating benefic as withdrawing protection.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Symbolic inference, not observed support.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is said to apply toward a square with Saturn in Cancer.
rules.original_source_qualifications: An approaching adverse aspect, no independent chart check.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly forecasts Parliament's soldiers essentially destroying the Queen's army.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Stronger categorical prediction than mere limited losses.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He anticipates a setback around the timing of that aspect.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No frozen tolerances for 'near'.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He recounts an episode on 11 April near Nottingham.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Year is not printed in that sentence; likely 1643 but preserve uncertainty.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The account says she lost some of her forces, not that the entire army was destroyed.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Explicit partial outcome and mismatch to categorical destruction.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: more had but knaves or fools
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims her losses could have been worse, blaming failings in Parliamentary forces.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Counterfactual partisan explanation, not observed proof of full destruction.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The following chapter begins a separate question about attaining a desired office.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Begins below divider on original PDF490.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: same time within four or five minutes
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The next inquirer asks within four or five minutes of the preceding figure's time.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Relative link between questions; does not supply missing absolute date of the preceding chart.
